text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- A member of the parliamentary Liberal party, Reinhard Firlinger, announced he will move to the far right Freedom Party.
- EA-Generali boss Dietrich Karner wants Die Erste savings bank to return to a consortium bidding for Creditanstalt.
- All the major parties want to reform the European Union, they said in Wednesday evening's televised debate ahead of EU parliamentary elections.
- Die Erste wants to push ahead with its plan for a joint holding for Creditanstalt and Die Erste. A new consortium might be put together.
- Austrian railways will order new trains worth 8 billion schillings.
- Vienna stock exchange expects to survive the introduction of the single currency.
- While new bidders are forming, Creditanstalt can present good results in its foreign business.
- Insurer EA-Generali does not expect any major short-term influences from the merger of Austrian insurers Bundeslaender and Austria-Collegialtaet.

- The Interior Ministry warns that the first letter bombs of the new series might arrive on Friday. The U.S. National Security Agency is helping the Austrian police to decipher a coded bomb threat, according to the paper.
- Erivan Haub, founder of retailer Tengelmann, is to decide on the future of Austria's Loewa this month.
- Die Erste is forming its own consortium to bid for Creditanstalt. Group could include German Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank, Swiss insurer Winterthur and Spanish Banco Santander.
- Philips plans to invest 100 million schillings in a new plant in Vienna.
